A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained content against additions and revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original training trajectories, weight-alignment measurements, optimizer-format experiments, downstream evaluations, and throughput and memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds extended training results, input-distribution and learning-rate analyses, Nvidia throughput measurements, and a GPT-3 experiment on C4.

M1.justification: Sections 4.4-5 retain the same Smooth-SwiGLU scaling procedure, inference folding, and E4M3/E5M2 Adam-moment formats. Newly disclosed master-weight details do not establish a procedural change; the Equation (1) revision concerns the theoretical setup.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds language-model pretraining on C4 using GPT-3 125M. RedPajama training and the Lambada, HellaSwag, Winogrande, ARC-C, and Wikitext evaluations remain. The added model sizes and hardware do not themselves expand task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 explicitly adds the variant retaining SwiGLU output in BF16 to the zero-shot comparison with BF16 and the proposed combination. This variant already appeared in v1's stability and throughput comparisons. v2 assigns the old FP8 scores to this variant and separately reports the combined method.

E3.justification: Figure 6 extends reported combined-method training from roughly 300B to 1.8T tokens. New protocols include Llama 700M BF16 experiments at three peak learning rates, a GPT-3 125M control, and measurements on eight Nvidia GPUs. TFLOPS becomes an additional performance metric. Figure 1 also revises its stated observation window from 128 to 50 iterations.

E4.justification: Beyond retained alignment and quantization analyses, v2 adds an outlier-input histogram probing the theoretical assumption (Figure 9), BF16 learning-rate sensitivity experiments (Figures 10-11), and training of a GPT-3/GeLU model without SwiGLU (Figure 12). These address additional mechanism and stability questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional curves and input histogram do not introduce run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantially longer training trajectories and new appendix findings. Table 2 retains but reattributes the old FP8 scores, then adds combined-method results including 62.1 Lambada and 65.43 Winogrande accuracy; these are not straightforward same-setting gains over the old row. Table 5 reports 4.32 versus 3.22 samples/sec for Smooth-SwiGLU versus BF16 on Nvidia hardware, a 34.16% increase. Gaudi throughput and memory values remain unchanged, while TFLOPS entries are added.

T1.justification: Equation (1) adds L2 regularization of the remaining network parameters, theta. The discussion following the proof also asserts applicability to other GLU variants. Theorem 1 and its central proof remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: trillion-token FP8 training, SwiGLU-driven outlier amplification, Smooth-SwiGLU, quantization of both Adam moments, BF16-comparable performance, and approximately 34% throughput improvement. Additional evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 changes the practical discussion from conditions holding for every sample to typically small sigmoid derivatives, adding a network-capacity argument and histogram evidence. Section 4.4 newly argues that RMSNorm and attention are not the instability source. Appendix A.3 interprets its results as showing BF16 stability and loss benefits.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reference-implementation URL and reproducibility statement, reports 15 days of training, and explicitly documents high-precision weight storage, delayed scaling, and FP16 master weights. The appendix also supplies hardware and learning-rate settings for its new experiments. Repository contents are not available as evidence within the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bondarenko et al. on quantizable transformers, Liu et al. on SpinQuant, and Sun et al. on massive activations, expanding the inference-outlier context. Its principal positioning relative to Peng et al.'s shorter FP8 training remains.

P1.justification: The main seven-section narrative is retained. Changes comprise targeted prose corrections and explanatory expansions, numbered optimizer subsections, new reproducibility and ethics paragraphs, acknowledgements, additional appendix subsections, and updated affiliations and conference headers.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual material with the input histogram, learning-rate panels and zoom, GPT-3 training curve, and Nvidia performance table. It also revises Figure 1's axis labels, extends Figure 6's time axis, adds a Table 2 row, and adds a TFLOPS column to Table 3.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly presented only roughly 300B tokens of combined-method training and promised additional steps despite its trillion-token claims. v2 substantially closes this validation gap with a curve reaching about 1.8T tokens and separately identified downstream results for the combined method. Added mechanism checks, learning-rate experiments, hardware measurements, and implementation information strengthen the evidence. The displayed combined-method curve still falls short of the exact 2T claim, and repeated-run uncertainty remains absent, but the central empirical support improves substantially.
